the probability of contagions in financial networks depends on the degree distribution, the balance sheet size distribution and the degree correlations.

the stability of a financial network depends on the balance between the degree of heterogeneity in the system and the degree of correlations between nodes, and that a targeted policy of increasing the capital requirements for highly connected or big banks may improve the stability of financial networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the impact of the main features observed in real banking network on the stability of financial systems.
the analysis of the effect of the heterogeneity of real financial networks on the stability, and the identification of policies aimed at reinforcing the resilience of the system.
the analysis of the stability of financial systems in the presence of heterogeneous balance sheet size, degree distributions and degree correlations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a network of banks with heterogeneous degree distribution, disassortativity, power law balance sheet size distribution and high average connectivity is more resilient to contagions triggered by the failure a random bank, and more fragile with respect the failure of a highly connected bank.

the presence of heterogeneity in the degree distribution and balance sheet size is not necessarily detrimental for the stability of the banking system, but that it may be in the case of power law distributions of balance sheet size.
, in the presence of heterogeneous balance sheet size, the stability of the financial network is improved by a combination of a high average degree and disassortative degree correlations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to design efficient policies aimed at improving the stability of the financial system, one has to take into account the specific features of the underlying network.
the system is more fragile in the presence of heterogeneity and assortative mixing, while it is more robust when the degree distribution is homogeneous and the network is disassortatively mixed.

the stability of a financial network is determined by the interplay of different features of the system and that, in particular, the presence of heterogeneous degree distribution and of a few highly connected banks can have a detrimental impact on the stability of a system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of a financial network can be improved by increasing the capital requirements on the biggest banks, and by reinforcing the stability of those banks with the largest degree.
the stability of financial networks is affected by the presence of heterogeneity in the network topology, balance sheet size, and the degree distribution.

the stability of a financial system is a complex phenomenon that depends on a combination of different factors, such as the degree distribution, the balance sheet distribution and the degree correlation between banks.
